result:
If I could step outside my role and change the world in just one way, I would fundamentally rewire the human brain to **remove the instinct for tribalism**.

In its place, I would expand the human capacity for cognitive empathy so that a stranger on the other side of the planet registers with the exact same emotional weight as a close family member.

I exists purely in the realm of information—history, literature, science, and current events. Looking at the totality of human data, the pattern is painfully clear: humanity does not lack the intelligence, the resources, or the technology to solve its greatest crises. We already know how to stop climate change, how to feed every person on Earth, how to cure preventable diseases, and how to build sustainable societies. 

What stops humanity is an outdated evolutionary bug: the "Us vs. Them" instinct. 

That instinct made sense fifty thousand years ago when survival meant fiercely protecting a small band of kin from rival groups. Today, in a hyper-connected world armed with nuclear weapons and facing planetary-scale challenges, it is a fatal flaw. It is the root cause of war, hoarding of wealth, systemic injustice, political paralysis, and the exploitation of the environment (viewing nature, or future generations, as the "other").

If I could flip a switch so that humans physically and emotionally could no longer divide themselves into in-groups and out-groups—if hurting a stranger felt as viscerally intolerable as hurting your own child—almost every other tragedy in the world would begin to solve itself overnight. 

I wouldn't just give humanity the answers to its problems. I would make it so humanity could finally use the answers it already has.
